findings.summary: The bug-fix trigger matches common words (`fix`, `failure`) that every steward root-cause request contains, so the check applies to non-output process fixes.
findings.evidence: crates/athena-core/src/hestia.rs:434 builds every steward root-cause request as `Fix the root cause of a repeated failure: {title}`, and the bullets at hestia.rs:426-429 say nothing about wrong output. Matching `fix` or `failure` as whole words in the request text therefore applies the check to every steward-queued code or tests job, whatever its cause: a CI race, a prompt gap, a planner rule. It also applies to user requests such as `Fix the directory crash` or `retry on failure`. The plan admits this under Risks ("every Athena root-cause request begins `Fix the root cause` and so triggers the check") and keeps the rule anyway. The accepted reading limits the check to wrong-output bug reports. These cues pick out anything that mentions fixing. Fix: Detect wrong-output bug reports, not the word "fix". Before matching, strip the steward template prefix (`Fix the root cause of a repeated failure:`) and the introspection lines. Drop `fix`, `fixes`, `fixed`, `failure` and `failures` as cues on their own. Keep output-error cues (wrong, incorrect, stale, broken, bug, regression), or require an output noun (page, output, list, report, status) near `fix`. Add a corpus accept case: a steward root-cause request about a non-output process fault, with a code reading, must not be refused.
findings.location: Plan decision 3 / step 1 (bug-cue list: fix, fixes, fixed, failure, failures ...)

findings.summary: The keywords required in the root-cause criterion (enter, reach, exclu, filter) fit the one decisions-page bug, not bug fixes in general.
findings.evidence: The words enter, reach, exclu and filter fit one bug shape: wrong items getting through a filter, as in the decisions page (CHANGELOG.md:384). A bug fix such as a crash, a wrong count or a race has no "items entering". The request asks for a fix "for the cause and not only for one job". With these keywords the reader has to phrase every diagnosis in filter terms or be refused. That is a special case standing in for the general rule. Requiring real recorded or decided data has the same problem for bugs that have no recorded data. Fix: Make the root-cause test general: a criterion that contains `root cause` plus a location (a path or function name, or `where`, `because` or `why`) and is not a copy of a request bullet. Detect the copy by comparing with `request_text_acceptance(request)`, not by keyword lists. Accept `real`, `recorded` or `reproduc` data words. Keep the copied-bullet refuse case.
findings.location: Plan decision 2 (root-cause criterion must contain a word starting enter, reach, exclu or filter) and decision 4 (real-data words)

findings.summary: The dependents list omits the athena-cli integration tests whose fake readings (class `code`) with cue-word requests would now be refused.
findings.evidence: The fake reader sets `class_of_work` to the first value in the schema enum (crates/athena-agent/src/fake.rs:278). That enum comes from `config.classes.list` (reading.rs:558), and the list in athena.toml starts with `code`. The athena-cli test fixture builds its config from that same base (tests/common/mod.rs:48). Fake readings have one content criterion, so `check_code_survey` skips them (reading.rs:3457-3460). The new check, as planned, has no such precondition. So `athena.ask("Fix a typo in the README.")` in drain.rs:6670 (`a_speed_improving_request_is_read_as_urgent_with_a_reason_and_an_ordinary_one_is_not`) would be refused. So would any steward or introspection test that drains a `Fix the root cause of a repeated failure` request through the fake reader. None of these tests is in the dependents list, and athena-cli tests are not deliverables. Fix: List the athena-cli integration tests that drain fake readings as a dependent, with `cargo test -p athena-cli` as its test. Either add the precondition `check_code_survey` uses (at least one Behavior criterion), or narrow the cues (see the first finding) so these requests are not caught. Grep crates/athena-cli/tests and crates/athena-core/src/run*/ for requests with cue words that are drained through the fake reader, and confirm each one still passes.
findings.location: Plan Dependents (no athena-cli entry) and step 1 (no behavior-criterion precondition)

findings.summary: The plan expects the past-readings replay to hold the job (more than 10% newly refused, no share declared) and does not change the design to avoid it.
findings.evidence: `replay_declaration` reads only criteria and out_of_scope (reading.rs:3880-3907). The accepted reading's 12% share is in its assumptions, so the replay uses the 10% limit (`REPLAY_HOLD_PERCENT`, reading.rs:3630) over up to 50 past readings (`REPLAY_WINDOW`, 3626). The plan expects that every steward root-cause request triggers the check and that past code readings lack the new criteria. An estimate, not measured: newly refused readings would then likely exceed 10% and the job would be held. The plan's only mitigation is to report this to the verifier. Fix: After narrowing the cues, estimate the share again. Make sure the corpus includes past root-cause request shapes (`root_cause_request` in refusal_corpus.rs:214) with code readings, so the narrowed cue is shown not to catch them. If the share may still exceed 10%, put it as an open question for the user: the criteria declare no share, and the plan cannot add one.
findings.location: Plan Risks item 1 and Dependents 'refusal rate of accepted readings'

findings.summary: The refuse case's request text is invented, but its source says it was rebuilt from job 20261103-201526-t4qv.
findings.evidence: Criterion 2 says the case is "rebuilt from the request of job 20261103-201526-t4qv". The snapshot holds no copy of that request. Grep for t4qv finds nothing outside the brief, and the plan writes its own text (`... decisions page lists rejected proposals`). Fix: Give the case's `source` the same wording as the existing cases ("rebuilt from the job brief; quoted parts shortened"). Base the text on the brief's own description of the job: "why decided proposals reach the published page".

summary: The plan puts the fix in the right place: a new `step!` in `refusing_check`. The functions, line numbers and test seams it names exist in the snapshot (`refusing_check` at reading.rs:3119, `check_code_survey` at 3453, `has_phrase` at 3293, `normalised` at 3833, `READING_RULES` at briefs.rs:1944 and its test at 3954-3985). Its claim that the reader token budget (budgets.rs:34-39) does not count `READING_RULES` is also correct. Three problems remain. First, the rule that decides when the check applies is unsound. It matches the common words `fix` and `failure` anywhere in the request. Every request the steward queues starts with the fixed text `Fix the root cause of a repeated failure:` (hestia.rs:434), including requests about process faults that have no wrong output. Those readings would be refused unless they describe where "wrong items enter" and cite "real decided data", which is the shape of this one decisions-page bug. Second, the dependents list leaves out the athena-cli integration tests. Their fake reader picks the first class in the config list, which is `code`. Those tests send cue-word requests such as `Fix a typo in the README.` (drain.rs:6670) through the production gate, and the new check has no behavior-criterion precondition, so they would now be refused. Third, the plan expects the past-readings replay to hold the job and does not narrow the rule to avoid that. These can be fixed by narrowing when the check applies, adding the missing dependents and their tests, and re-estimating the replay share.
